subject: Re: Questions on data movement routing, PII classification, and KMS custody
messages:
From: Luke Mercer <l.mercer@medilink.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Anna Choi <anna.choi@medilink.com>, data-privacy@medilink.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Questions on routing / PII classification / KMS custody

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick discussions last week. As we prepare our security review for the procurement team, a couple of items popped up that we need clarified before we circulate the DPA exhibit to legal:

- Can you confirm where tokenized PII may transit (regions / cloud egress)? We need a clear map of which requests are routed through non-EU regions for fallback/burst.
- For customer-managed encryption keys: do you support BYOK (customer KMS) for the models that will process our PHI-scope PII, or is Redwood KMS-only for hosted deployments?
- Please provide the current subprocessors list and a short mapping of which subprocessor touches unredacted PII, pseudonymized outputs, or only aggregated telemetry.
- We would like a simple data movement diagram (ingest -> processing -> cache -> logs/exports) with custody annotations (who holds keys, whether KV cache stores plaintext, etc.).
- Finally, any standard contractual mechanism you support for transfers (SCCs, UK Addendum, or equivalent) and estimated timing for Exhibit C redlines.

Apologies for the list — the procurement / security teams are strict since this is a regulated payer workflow. Could you send answers and a diagram by end of week?

Thanks,
Luke
Luke Mercer
Security & Risk, MediLink Health
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Luke Mercer <l.mercer@medilink.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on routing / PII classification / KMS custody

Hi Luke — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the information you need; summarize below and I attached a first-pass diagram and a working mapping for subprocessors. Internal team, please see notes and correct as needed.

1) Regional routing and fallback
- Primary processing for MediLink will be pinned to our eu-west region (Frankfurt).
- Fallback behavior: in the event of capacity constraints we may route to eu-central first, then to a dedicated 'burst' pool in the eu region. We do not route request payloads to non-EU regions for your account unless you explicitly authorize a cross-border exception.

2) Customer-managed keys (BYOK)
- We support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts we offer a customer-managed KMS option (BYOK) as part of Enterprise onboarding — keys remain in your KMS and we use an envelope-wrapping flow. Note: BYOK for hosted requires an onboarding window to configure key grants.

3) Subprocessors mapping
- See attached subprocessors_mapping.csv for current roster and a column indicating data exposure category: "unredacted-PII", "pseudonymized", "aggregated-telemetry".

4) Data movement diagram
- Attached: redwood-dataflow-v2.png (simple ingest -> preprocess -> KV-cache -> model-serving -> audit-export). Custody notes are annotated (keys: customer controlled for BYOK, KV cache encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys; ephemeral plaintext in GPU memory only during inference).

5) Transfers & contractual mechanisms
- We support EU SCCs and UK Addendum; we can offer those as a standard attachment. For MediLink we recommend adding the Exhibit C redline we prepared (attached) to speed legal review.

Next steps: Jordan — can you confirm the KV cache retention window defaults we can offer for this account and whether we can lower it to 1 hour for PHI-scoped traffic? Grace — please confirm subprocessors CSV accuracy.

I'll follow up with a consolidated Exhibit C redline and a link to a shared Drive doc for comments.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Privacy Programs, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-dataflow-v2.png (image/png)
Attachment: subprocessors_mapping.csv (text/csv)
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on routing / PII classification / KMS custody

On Wed, 10 Jun 2026 at 13:45, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> 1) Regional routing and fallback
> - Primary processing for MediLink will be pinned to our eu-west region (Frankfurt).
> - Fallback behavior...

Kimberly — quick internal notes and proposals:

- KV cache retention: we can offer a configurable retention window; default is 24h but for regulated customers we can set to 1 hour for a per-account policy. Need ops sign-off for permanent reduction but can do as a contractual SLA during onboarding.
- GPU memory: confirm ephemeral only; we do not persist plaintext to disk. Will add exact language around eviction and max residency time (we should state <30s for typical inference spans, call out worst-case locks if batching).
- Subprocessors: current list in CSV includes cloud infra partner (region-specific), monitoring vendor (aggregated only), and a tracing provider (pseudonymized). Grace — please verify column "data_exposure" before we send to MediLink.
- Transfers: SCCs ready; for faster turnaround propose we send pre-filled SCC template + UK Addendum and mark Exhibit C with our standard encryption and key custody clauses.

I'll prepare the short ops FAQ snippet on cache and key custody for Kimberly to send.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Infra PM, Redwood Inference
From: Luke Mercer <l.mercer@medilink.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Anna Choi <anna.choi@medilink.com>, data-privacy@medilink.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on routing / PII classification / KMS custody

Kimberly, Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing the diagram and CSV: 

- Encryption in transit: can you confirm that TLS 1.2+ is enforced and whether mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for customer endpoints? Our infra team prefers mTLS for API calls from our ETL to your ingest layer.
- KV cache encryption: you mentioned per-tenant keys — are those keys customer-controlled under BYOK or managed by Redwood for hosted? If managed by Redwood, can we at least get attestations and rotation policy?
- Retention SLAs: will you commit to the 1-hour KV cache retention in contract for PHI-flagged traffic? If not full contract language, a temporary commitment while we complete a Dedicated onboarding would suffice.

Also copying Anna (legal) — she has a few redlines on Exhibit C later today. Can we expect a revised Exhibit C by tomorrow EOD?

Best,
Luke
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Luke Mercer <l.mercer@medilink.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on routing / PII classification / KMS custody

Hi Luke and Anna — answers consolidated below and next steps. See attached PDF with our proposed Exhibit C redlines.

- TLS / mTLS: We enforce TLS 1.2+ across all transport. mTLS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted API we can enable mTLS on a per-account basis as part of enterprise onboarding; it requires a brief key exchange and certificate pinning step.

- KV cache keys: For BYOK customers the per-tenant encryption key that wraps the KV cache encryption key is customer-controlled. For standard hosted (no BYOK) the keys are Redwood-managed; we provide quarterly rotation attestations and can provide a key lifecycle / rotation policy document.

- Retention SLA: We will commit to a 1-hour KV cache retention SLA for PHI-flagged traffic as a contractual Exhibit (subject to onboarding checklist). Implementation note: this will be enforced via per-tenant policy and audited in the Console.

- Exhibit C redlines and timeline: attached is dpa-exhibit-C-proposed-redlines.pdf. If MediLink returns final comments by Monday EOD we can route for legal approval and provide counters within 3 business days. DocuSign link will be provided after counters.

Next steps:
1) Anna/legal to send redlines to the Drive doc (link below) — we will track comments inline.
2) Ops (Jordan) to confirm implementation schedule for KV retention policy change and mTLS onboarding window.
3) Kimberly to share final SCC template and UK Addendum in the Drive.

Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcdExampleDriveLink
Doc attachments: dpa-exhibit-C-proposed-redlines.pdf, redwood-dataflow-v2.png, subprocessors_mapping.csv

Thanks — we aim to have the Exhibit C ready for signature within the week if comments are modest.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Privacy Programs, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
